Ṣaṇḍa, pl. (°āḥ), a people. § 574 (Jambūkh.): VI, 9μ, 351 (only C., B. has Saṇḍāḥ).

षष्टी: Ṣaṣṭī, a goddess. § 270 (Brahmasabhāv.): II, 11, 458 (in the palace of Brahmán).—§ 501 (Skandop.): III, 229, 14451 (among the names of Devasenā).
षोडशराजकपर्व: Ṣoḍaśarājaka(ṃ) parva. § 10 (Parvasaṅgr.): I, 2, 332 (p°. S°ṃ, i.e. Ṣoḍaśarājika, in the enumeration of parvans erroneously entered among those of the fifth book).
षोडशराजिक: [Ṣoḍaśarājika (ṃ)] (“the section relating to the sixteen kings”). § 595 (cf. Sṛñjaya). Nārada told Sṛñjaya the stories of the following kings: 1) Marutta (q.v.) (VII, 55); 2) Suhotra (q.v.) (VII, 56); 3) Paurava (q.v.) (VII, 57); 4) Śihi (q.v.) (VII, 58); 5) Rāma Dāśarathi (q.v.) (VII, 59); 6) Bhagīratha (q.v.) (VII, 60); 7) Dilīpa (q.v.) (VII, 61); 8) Māndhātṛ (q.v.) (VII, 62); 9) Yayāti (q.v.) (VII, 63); 10) Ambarīṣa (q.v.) (VII, 64); 11) Śaśabindu (q.v.) (VII, 65); 12) Gaya (q.v.) (VII, 66); 13) Rantideva (q.v.) (VII, 67); 14) Bharata Dauṣmanti (q.v.) (VII, 68); 15) Pṛthu Vainya (q.v.) (VII, 69); 16) Rāma Jāmadagnya (q.v.) (VII, 70).
षोडशराजोपाख्यान: [Ṣoḍaśarājopākhyāna(ṃ)] (“the episode relating to the sixteen kings,” XII, 29). § 632b (Rājadh.). The histories of the same sixteen kings as in Ṣoḍaśarājika (§ 595), except that Paurava is here named Bṛhadratha (“the Aṅga king”) and Rāma Jāmadagnya is replaced by Sagara (q.v.).
